title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
abstract: arXiv:2611.27180v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models(LLM) show promise for strategic reasoning, yet their ability to compute game-theoretic equilibria under dynamic conditions remains largely unexplored. This work investigates whether fine-tuned LLMs can serve as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation in honeypot allocation, a setting in which network mobility continuously reshapes the underlying attack graph and forces repeated re-solving of a two-player zero-sum game. We construct a dataset of 270 security games on networks of 8--25 nodes with solver-grounded equilibrium labels, and evaluate four classes of predictor over 1{,}524 held-out mobility events: non-learned baselines, six open-weight architectures evaluated zero-shot, the same six after LoRA fine-tuning, and four proprietary models as an external reference point. Predictions are scored without post-hoc repair against exact game-theoretic criteria: exploitability against an optimal attack

translated_title: 学习自适应防御策略：面向网络移动性下网络安全博弈的微调大语言模型
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在战略推理方面展现出潜力，但其在动态条件下计算博弈论均衡的能力在很大程度上仍未被探索。本研究探讨了微调后的LLM能否作为无需求解器的替代方案，用于蜜罐分配场景中的在线均衡计算——在该场景下，网络移动性会持续重塑底层攻击图，迫使双人零和博弈不断重新求解。我们构建了一个包含270个安全博弈的数据集（覆盖8至25个节点的网络，并带有基于求解器计算得到的均衡标签），并在1,524个留出的移动性事件上评估了四类预测器：非学习型基线、六个开源权重架构的零样本表现、经过LoRA微调后的同六个模型，以及作为外部参考的四个专有模型。所有预测均无需事后修复，直接依据精确的博弈论标准进行评分：即面对最优攻击时的可利用性……
tldr: 本研究构建了带有求解器均衡标签的270个蜜罐分配安全博弈数据集，首次系统评估了LoRA微调的大语言模型能否在网络移动性持续改变攻击图的动态场景下，充当无需求解器的在线博弈均衡计算替代方案。
en_tdlr: This work constructs a dataset of 270 honeypot-allocation security games with solver-grounded equilibrium labels and systematically evaluates whether LoRA fine-tuned LLMs can serve as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation under continuous network mobility.
